question.text: How should a quilt system use its cells' double-entry book-keeping (receipt chains) to rewind, snapshot, and save the state of individual cells, groups of cells (organs), or an entire quilt, so the saved state is a bootable drop-in that can nest inside another program or quilt? Specify the mechanisms, invariants, and failure modes.

pipeline.compose_test_separation: no model judges a node set it composed; flash cross-reviewed typesafe-only nodes; typesafe+hermes judged flash-merged nodes

nodes.title: Receipt row and canonical hash
nodes.content: Each cell appends rows with before/after, cause, deps, prev hash; canonical encoding gives stable SHA-256.

nodes.title: Verified tip and pruning
nodes.content: Boot rebuilds tip by verifying chain from anchor; pruning keeps checkpoint chain to live tip.

nodes.title: Single-cell rewind
nodes.content: Rewind appends new receipt with before=tip.after, after=target.after; old receipts remain.

nodes.title: Dependents stale on rewind
nodes.content: Reverse deps index marks consumers of superseded receipts stale; they must re-evaluate or rewind.

nodes.title: Snapshot under lease
nodes.content: Snapshot pins tip seq/hash and after-image under mutex or read lease; MVCC can avoid stop.

nodes.title: Bootable cell drop-in
nodes.content: Package snapshot, receipt log, schema, API manifest; loader verifies chain before instantiating.

nodes.title: Nesting imported cell via adapter
nodes.content: Host imports cell as boundary; writes import record; host inputs become receipts with cause host_input; nested chain stays authoritative.
nodes.faulty_note: minor: Fails to mention that nested cell writes require namespacing to avoid ID collisions

nodes.title: Organ ledger durability
nodes.content: Organ manifest lists member tips; ledger hashes cut; fsync cell logs before organ commit.

nodes.title: Organ rewind two-phase
nodes.content: Intent row then member rewinds; commit only when all tips match target cut.

nodes.title: Organ snapshot causal cut
nodes.content: Write barrier records member tip vector and causally closed dependency cut.

nodes.title: Bootable organ drop-in
nodes.content: Loader verifies all member chains and organ ledger hash; refuses boot on any mismatch.

nodes.title: Nest organ sub-quilt
nodes.content: Host namespaces member IDs and maps only exports; boundary inputs are receipts inside sub-quilt.

nodes.title: Quilt global ledger
nodes.content: Global ledger rows chain global cut vectors across all cells and organs.

nodes.title: Hierarchical quilt rewind
nodes.content: Every organ rewinds to prior cut; global commit only when all organs and cells match.

nodes.title: Epoch-barrier quilt snapshot
nodes.content: Increment epoch, barrier in-flight receipts, record single causal global cut.

nodes.title: Bootable quilt drop-in
nodes.content: Loader verifies all chains, ledgers, wires deps, starts scheduler after verification.

nodes.title: Nest whole quilt adapter
nodes.content: Adapter exposes exports; parent pins child outputs by receipt hash in boundary ledger.

nodes.title: Rewind dependency ripple
nodes.content: Producer rewind makes consumer pins superseded; append dep_rewound receipts or freeze.

nodes.title: External dependencies pinned by content hash
nodes.content: Bootable save records external_pins name, content_hash, version, URI. Loader checks hashes before wiring; mutable paths alone undetectable.

nodes.title: Hash and schema migration recorded as receipts
nodes.content: Receipts carry hash_algo and schema tags. Migrations are new receipts or anchors with schema_migration cause; silent changes break chains.

nodes.title: Reconcile partial commits
nodes.content: Intent logs scanned against tips to commit or compensate, ensuring one terminal row.

nodes.title: Namespacing prevents nested ID collisions
nodes.content: Nested IDs rewritten as subquilt_id plus cell_id, and receipt hashes include namespaced ID. Unqualified IDs can collide and corrupt wiring.

nodes.title: Parent-child composite snapshot
nodes.content: Parent records child manifest hash and cut; child verified before parent dependents wire.

nodes.title: Save nondeterministic runtime state explicitly
nodes.content: RNG seeds, timers, queues, clocks are special cells or manifest fields. Omitting seed diverges post-boot receipts.

nodes.title: Repeated core invariants
nodes.content: Append-only hash chains, new receipts for changes, content-addressed cuts, atomic group commits, verified boot.

nodes.title: Receipts prove local history only
nodes.content: Chains prove local history only; cross-cell consistency, access, liveness, availability need organ/global ledgers, intent logs, pins, verifiers, namespaces.

nodes.title: Receipt row and tip verification
nodes.content: Receipt row stores before/after images, cause_ref, deps_map; hash covers canonical fields. Boot verifies hash links to anchor, quarantines gaps.

nodes.title: Single-cell snapshot and drop-in
nodes.content: Snapshot exports immutable tip_hash, after_image, chain proof under lease. Drop-in packages snapshot, receipt log, schema, manifest; loader verifies before instantiating.

nodes.title: Organ snapshot acquires write barrier
nodes.content: Organ snapshot archives manifest, member snapshots, logs, external pins, ledger slice. Write barrier freezes members; cut must be causally closed.

nodes.title: Organ nested via namespace exports
nodes.content: Sub-quilt imports organ under namespace prefix and maps only manifest exports. Host bypassing exports causes non-linearized cross-ledger writes.

nodes.title: Quilt ledger global cut
nodes.content: Hash-chained quilt_ledger rows carry global cut vector and monotonic global_epoch. Cut is one causal line, not wall-clock grouping.

nodes.title: Quilt snapshot and bootable drop-in
nodes.content: Quilt snapshot increments epoch, waits, records one global cut. Drop-in verifies all chains and ledgers before scheduler.

nodes.title: Pruning trades rewind depth for storage
nodes.content: Cells keep log tail plus checkpoint; old receipts go cold. Missing checkpoint blocks deep rewind and audit.

nodes.title: Crash atomic fsync order
nodes.content: Fsync cell logs before organ commit, organ commits before global commit. Reversed order commits rows to unflushed tips.

nodes.title: Canonical serialization stabilizes receipt hashes
nodes.content: Canonical CBOR with sorted keys and schema version ensures identical logical state reproduces same hash. Non-determinism forks verification.

nodes.title: Concurrent snapshot linearization
nodes.content: Per-cell mutexes and read leases produce a linearized cut; mutations block or fail. Unblocked mutations can mix tips never coexisting.

nodes.title: Partial commit reconciliation
nodes.content: Multi-cell transactions start in intent log; recovery scans intents against cell tips and commits or compensates. No uncommitted intermediate tips.

nodes.title: Invariants repeat at every granularity
nodes.content: Chains append-only; every change new receipt; snapshots content-addressed; group commits atomic; dependencies hash-pinned; boot verifies before instantiate. Breaks quarantine level.

nodes.title: Receipt row double entry
nodes.content: Per-cell append-only row stores before, after, cause, deps, prev_hash, and SHA-256 over canonical fields; images grow logs without deltas.

nodes.title: Tip boot verification quarantine
nodes.content: Committed tip is highest verified after_image; boot checks prev_hash links from anchor. Gaps quarantine cell, forbidding suspect tail boot.

nodes.title: Single cell snapshot lease
nodes.content: Snapshot is content-addressed record with tip_seq, tip_hash, after_image, and chain proof. Per-cell lease prevents torn tip-image mismatch.

nodes.title: Single cell drop in
nodes.content: Drop-in packages snapshot, receipt log, schema, and pins. Loader verifies log and tip_hash before instantiation; redaction is signed receipt variant.

nodes.title: Cell nesting import record
nodes.content: Host imports cell as boundary, journals imported tip_hash, and writes host inputs as nested receipts. Concurrent writers serialize on prev_hash.

nodes.title: Organ manifest ledger
nodes.content: Organ manifest pins member tips and ledger hash. Append-only organ_ledger rows carry cut_vector; tampering any member tip breaks organ hash.

nodes.title: Organ rewind two phase
nodes.content: Intent row prepares group rewind; members append in order, commit records new cut. Crash leaves partial; recovery completes or compensates.

nodes.title: Quilt snapshot epoch barrier
nodes.content: Snapshot increments global_epoch, waits for in-flight receipts, records global cut. MVCC reads old tips while new writes continue past cut.

nodes.title: Quilt drop in nondeterminism
nodes.content: Quilt drop-in loader verifies all chains and ledgers before scheduler. Saved RNG seeds, timers, and clocks prevent post-boot divergence.

nodes.title: Pruning checkpoint cold storage
nodes.content: Live tip chains to last checkpoint hash; old receipts move to cold storage. Corrupt checkpoint disables deep rewind and audit.

nodes.title: Organ nested via namespace exports
nodes.content: Sub-quilt imports organ under namespace prefix and maps only manifest exports. Host bypassing exports causes non-linearized cross-ledger writes.

rejected.title: point P1 (jev load 0.57)
rejected.content: P1. A cell's receipt chain is a per-cell append-only ledger row `(cell_id, seq, prev_hash, before_image, after_image, cause_ref, deps_map, wall_clock, hash)` where `hash = SHA-256(cell_id || seq || prev_hash || canonical(before_image) || canonical(after_image) || canonical(cause_ref) || canonical(deps_map))`. The double-entry property means every row stores both before and after states plus the triggering cause and exact dependency versions, making changes auditable and reversible.

rejected.title: point P2 (jev load 0.61)
rejected.content: P2. A cell's committed current state is `tip.after_image`, where the tip is the highest-`seq` receipt whose chain verifies from a trusted anchor/genesis. Boot rebuilds `cell_tip = (seq, hash, after_image_ref)` by scanning `receipt_log` and checking `receipt[k].prev_hash == receipt[k-1].hash`.

rejected.title: point P3 (jev load 0.55)
rejected.content: P3. Single-cell rewind uses the receipt chain as an append-only time machine: locate the target receipt `R_t` by `seq` or `hash`, verify it back to the anchor, read current tip `R_cur`, then append `R_rw = (cell_id, tip.seq+1, tip.hash, before=tip.after, after=R_t.after, cause={"op":"rewind","target_receipt":R_t.hash}, deps=R_t.deps, ts=now, hash=...)`. Invariant: old receipts are never deleted; the rewind is just a new valid transition whose `after_image` equals the target's `after_image`.

rejected.title: point P4 (jev load 0.55)
rejected.content: P4. Single-cell rewind must account for dependents, not just the rewound cell. The runtime keeps `dep_index[ (cell_id, receipt_hash) ] -> [dependent_receipt_ids]` built from each receipt's `deps_map`.

rejected.title: point P5 (jev load 0.43)
rejected.content: P5. A single-cell snapshot is an immutable export record `cell_snapshot.json = {schema_version, cell_id, tip_seq, tip_hash, after_image, prev_hash, proof_type, chain_proof, dep_pins, created_at}`. To make it, the cell is read under its per-cell mutex or a read lease, and the snapshot is content-addressed by `file_sha256`; the included proof is the ordered receipt headers from anchor to tip, or a Merkle path if the ledger is Merkelized.

rejected.title: point P6 (jev load 0.54)
rejected.content: P6. A single-cell bootable drop-in packages `cell_drop_in/` with `cell_snapshot.json`, `receipt_log.cbor`, `schema.cbor`, `api_manifest.json`, and `dep_pins.json`. On load, the host verifies the receipt log, recomputes `tip_hash`, compares it to the snapshot, then instantiates the cell with `state = tip.after_image`; the first future mutation appends a receipt with `prev_hash = tip.hash`.

rejected.title: point P7 (jev load 0.66)
rejected.content: P7. To nest a single saved cell in a host quilt, the host imports it as a boundary cell and writes an import record `{host_cell_id, imported_cell_id, imported_tip_hash, content_hash, mapping}` into its import journal. Host inputs become normal receipts in the nested cell's log with `cause={"type":"host_input","host_txn_id":...}`; host reads pin the exact nested receipt hash/content hash.

rejected.title: point P8 (jev load 0.57)
rejected.content: P8. An organ is defined by `organ_manifest.json = {organ_id, version, members:[{cell_id, role, tip_hash, seq}], organ_ledger_hash, external_pins, exports}`. Its group-level bookkeeping is an append-only hash-chained file `organ_ledger.jsonl`; rows are `(ledger_seq, prev_ledger_hash, txn_id, type, cut_vector, cause, ts, hash)` where `cut_vector = {cell_id: tip_hash}`.

rejected.title: point P9 (jev load 0.46)
rejected.content: P9. Organ rewind is a two-phase group transaction. It writes an `organ_intent.jsonl` row `{txn_id, type:"rewind", target_cut:T, status:"preparing"}`, then for each member cell in deterministic order appends a cell rewind receipt to the target cut.

rejected.title: point P10 (jev load 0.42)
rejected.content: P10. An organ snapshot is an archive `organ_snapshot/` containing `manifest.json`, per-member `cell_snapshot.json` files, member receipt logs, `external_pins.json`, and an `organ_ledger_slice.jsonl` up to the cut. Snapshot capture first acquires the organ write barrier so no member appends during the cut, then records the member tip vector.

rejected.title: point P11 (jev load 0.38)
rejected.content: P11. An organ saved as a bootable drop-in is the organ snapshot plus a loader manifest giving init order and public API. The loader verifies every member cell chain and the organ ledger hash before instantiating any member; if one member fails, the whole organ refuses to boot.

rejected.title: point P13 (jev load 0.49)
rejected.content: P13. Whole-quilt coordination uses a hash-chained `quilt_ledger.jsonl` with rows `(global_seq, prev_global_hash, txn_id, type, global_cut_vector, organ_cut_vectors, cause, ts, hash)` and a monotonic `global_epoch`. The global cut vector is the set of all cell tips or all organ tip vectors across the quilt.

rejected.title: point P14 (jev load 0.41)
rejected.content: P14. Whole-quilt rewind uses hierarchical two-phase commit: choose a prior global cut from `quilt_ledger.jsonl`, have every organ execute its organ rewind to that cut, then append a `type:"rewind_commit"` global ledger row with the new global cut vector. Invariant: the quilt is committed only when every organ ledger and every member cell is at the designated tip.

rejected.title: point P15 (jev load 0.44)
rejected.content: P15. A whole-quilt snapshot is a directory `quilt_snapshot/` with `quilt_manifest.json`, per-organ or per-cell snapshots, receipt logs, `external_pins.json`, and a `global_ledger_slice.jsonl`. Snapshot capture increments `global_epoch`, waits for all in-flight receipts to land before the epoch barrier, then records the resulting global cut.

rejected.title: point P16 (jev load 0.47)
rejected.content: P16. A whole-quilt bootable drop-in packages the global snapshot plus runtime config and bootstrap order. On boot the loader verifies all cell receipt chains, organ ledgers, and the global ledger hash, instantiates cells, wires dependencies from `deps_map`, and only then starts the scheduler.

rejected.title: point P17 (jev load 0.59)
rejected.content: P17. Nesting a whole quilt as a sub-quilt requires an adapter that exposes only the saved quilt's `exports`. The parent records each boundary interaction in a `boundary_ledger`; an input into the sub-quilt becomes a receipt in the target sub-quilt cell with `cause={"type":"parent_input","parent_receipt_hash":...}`, and an output read by the parent is pinned by the sub-quilt receipt hash.

rejected.title: point P18 (jev load 0.36)
rejected.content: P18. Pruning is a storage failure mode. Because rewind depth depends on retained receipts, a cell may keep only a recent log tail plus a checkpoint snapshot; old receipts move to cold storage keyed by `(cell_id, receipt_hash)`.

rejected.title: point P19 (jev load 0.34)
rejected.content: P19. Rewinding one cell can ripple through dependents. A cell's receipt `deps_map` pins another cell by `receipt_hash`; when the producer is rewound, the consumer's pin points to a superseded historical receipt.

rejected.title: point P20 (jev load 0.23)
rejected.content: P20. Organ and global ledgers require crash-atomic ordering with cell logs. The rule is: fsync member cell receipt logs before fsyncing the organ commit row, and fsync organ commits before fsyncing the global quilt commit row.

rejected.title: point P21 (jev load 0.4)
rejected.content: P21. External dependencies must be pinned by content hash. A bootable save records `external_pins.json` as `{name, content_hash, version, retrieval_uri}`; at load, the runtime checks hashes of any loaded dependency before wiring it.

rejected.title: point P22 (jev load 0.35)
rejected.content: P22. Chain integrity depends on deterministic serialization. Before/after images and receipt fields must be encoded with a stable canonical format such as canonical CBOR with sorted keys and explicit schema version.

rejected.title: point P23 (jev load 0.4)
rejected.content: P23. Concurrent snapshot/rewind writes are controlled by per-cell mutexes and version checks. A global or organ snapshot acquires read leases on all member cells to produce a linearized cut; mutations either block or fail.

rejected.title: point P24 (jev load 0.28)
rejected.content: P24. Hash algorithm and schema evolution are failure modes. Receipts should include an algorithm tag or domain separator per cell/organ schema version, e.g.

rejected.title: point P25 (jev load 0.35)
rejected.content: P25. Partial commit reconciliation handles failures in multi-cell operations. Every organ/global transaction starts in an intent log; recovery scans intents against current cell tips and commits or compensates.

rejected.title: point P26 (jev load 0.5)
rejected.content: P26. Namespacing is a nesting failure mode. Nested cell IDs must be rewritten as `subquilt_id + cell_id`, and receipt hashes must include the namespaced cell ID so identical local IDs cannot collide.

rejected.title: point P27 (jev load 0.34)
rejected.content: P27. Composite parent-child snapshot is a nesting-specific failure. If a parent quilt depends on a child sub-quilt's exported receipt hash, the parent snapshot must also record the child drop-in's manifest hash and cut vector.

rejected.title: point P28 (jev load 0.51)
rejected.content: P28. Non-deterministic runtime state must be saved explicitly. Random seeds, timers, network pending queues, and monotonic clocks are not reconstructible from receipt after-images alone, so they must be represented as special cells or manifest fields.

rejected.title: point P29 (jev load 0.12)
rejected.content: P29. The central invariants repeat at every granularity: receipt chains are append-only and hash-linked; every state change, including rewind, restore, and import, is a new receipt; snapshots are content-addressed cuts; group commits are atomic across members; dependencies are pinned by receipt hash or content hash rather than mutable pointers; and boot always verifies before instantiating. Failure at any level is containment: a single cell hash break quarantines that cell, an organ hash break quarantines the organ, and a global cut mismatch quarantines the whole quilt.

rejected.title: point P30 (jev load 0.15)
rejected.content: P30. The overall failure boundary is that receipt chains prove local history but do not by themselves enforce cross-cell consistency, access control, liveness, or external availability. Those require the organ/global ledgers, intent logs, content-pinned external manifests, boot verifiers, and namespace/export boundaries described above.

hermes.rationale: Graph covers key mechanisms but omits some failure modes like ID collisions when nesting. Overall quite thorough.
